newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen probing above 117 yen in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen probing above 117 yen in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is expected to maintain its bullish tone against the yen and the mark in Asia on Monday, and is seen probing above 117 yen, dealers said.
The underlying trend turned stronger after the dollar breached 116.50 yen last Friday, but exporters are expected to sell on rallies, with offers lined up around 117.20/30 yen.
"The dollar is expected to be well-supported around 116.50 yen. Market sentiment turned even stronger after rising above that level," a Japanese city bank dealer said.
"But we want to see whether Japanese exporters will sell actively in Tokyo today," he said.

Dealers said the dollar was expected to maintain its bullishness against the mark, but the market was becoming concerned about the dollar's rapid rise after comments made by the Bundesbank officials last Friday.
"Dollar/mark is bullish, but I wouldn't be too surprised to see a slight downward correction and the dollar capped lightly above 1.84 marks today," the dealer said.

Bundesbank Vice President Johann Wilhelm Gaddum was quoted in a European weekly newspaper on Friday as saying that the dollar was slightly overvalued against the mark, but that mark weakness was not sparking inflationary pressures in Germany.

Meanwhile, Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen told a German daily that central bank policymakers were "driving carefully" in the current exchange rate environment, and suggested that the Bundesbank wanted to send a signal to the market by setting its repo rate at a fixed level for only a portion of the current recess period.

"Although the mark's recovery has been limited after a series of comments by German officials, the market could be a little concerned about aggressive (mark) selling from 1.84 marks (against the dollar)," a Japanese trust bank dealer said.
Dealers expect the dollar to be capped around 1.8420 marks, while it is likely to be supported around 1.8330 in Asia.
On Friday, the greenback rose as high as 1.8405 marks in late Tokyo trade, its highest level since July 1991.
